statements.impact_statement: CVE-2026-8925: curl's SASL code could clean up its GSASL context twice without clearing the pointer in between, freeing the same memory twice during IMAP, POP3 or SMTP authentication (https://curl.se/docs/CVE-2026-8925.html). curl's advisory says the flaw can trigger only when curl is built to use libgsasl. It affects curl 8.15.0 to 8.20.0 and was fixed in curl 8.21.0 by https://github.com/curl/curl/commit/3da249e1f0716c06644ed3522a37a8bf81808012, whose only code change is in lib/vauth/gsasl.c, a file compiled only when libgsasl support is enabled. The DHI curl packages for Alpine 3.23 are builds of curl 8.17.0-r1, 8.18.0-r0 (in both the main and the security repository), 8.19.0-r0, 8.20.0-r0, 8.20.0-r1, 8.21.0-r0, 8.22.0-r0, 8.23.0-r0 and 8.23.0-r1, and the version string in each build's libcurl matches its package version. In the libcurl, curl and curl-static packages of every one of these builds, on x86_64 and aarch64, neither libcurl.so.4 nor the curl program lists libgsasl as a NEEDED library, and the static libcurl.a defines none of the Curl_auth_gsasl_* functions and references no gsasl_* symbol, while the same symbol search finds Curl_sasl_start and Curl_auth_create_plain_message defined in each build. libgsasl support is not built, so the vulnerable code is not present.
